subjects.title: Which ZIA log fields are not logged until enabled

claims.statement: Logging of the web log client source port, clt_sport, is enabled by contacting Zscaler Support.
df_hostname is populated only when TLS Inspection is enabled.
Logging of the DLP Allowed Rule Name, dlprulename, is enabled by contacting Zscaler Support.
The firewall log lists csport and sdport with no enablement note in its field CSV, while the web log lists the client source port and server destination port as needing Support to enable.
Logging of the web log server destination port, srv_dport, is enabled by contacting Zscaler Support.

subjects.title: What a ZIA firewall log record is: aggregates, action and field names

claims.statement: Similar fields are named differently in the firewall and web logs: ttype and trafficredirectmethod, external_deviceid and external_devid, bypass_etime and bypassed_etime, bypassed_session and bypassed_traffic, and threat_severity and threatseverity.

The firewall rulelabel is described as the rule applied to the transaction with no Block-only qualifier, unlike the web log rulelabel, which applies only to Block rules; its example is the Default Firewall Filtering Rule.

subjects.title: How NSS feeds encode and deliver ZIA log fields

claims.statement: The eedone field, specific to NSS, indicates whether the characters in the feed's Feed Escape Character field were hex encoded.
The tz field is the time zone specified when the NSS feed was configured, and the time field excludes the time zone.
The service hex encodes URL characters at or below 0x20 or at or above 0x7F as %HH when it sends logs to NSS, so a space in a URL arrives as %20 and a newline as %0A.

subjects.title: Value encodings and caveats of ZIA web log fields

claims.statement: bypassed_traffic is a numeric flag where 1 means the traffic bypassed Zscaler Client Connector.

The cip field is the internal client IP when it is visible, for example through a GRE tunnel or an XFF header, and otherwise equals cintip; cintip is the NATed public IP and differs from cip only when the internal address is visible.
dlprulename applies only to Allow rules; trig_dlprulename names the DLP rule that triggered the transaction, allowed or blocked; all_dlprulenames combines other_dlprulenames and trig_dlprulename.

df_hostname holds the TLS SNI when it differs from the HTTPS Host header, and df_hosthead marks an FQDN mismatch between the request URL and the Host header; each appears only when there is a mismatch.
The host field takes the host value from the HTTP request line when present and the Host header otherwise.
For traffic processed through Isolation, userlocationname holds the actual origination point while location holds the Isolation Location; for other traffic userlocationname is None.
malwarecat holds the malware category detected in the transaction and also indicates whether a file was submitted to the Sandbox engine and the analysis result.
app_risk_score displays None when the risk index is unavailable, and ua_token displays None when no user agent token exists.
The reason field's documentation refers readers to the Policy Reasons article for the reasons behind policy actions.
The respcode field is the response code sent to the client, and the service generates a 403 Forbidden response for blocked transactions.
A 403 in respcode on a blocked transaction is the service's own response and does not show that the origin server answered 403.
The service computes the Page Risk Index for each page by weighing page locations, destination reputation and suspicious-looking content, on a 0 to 100 scale from lowest to highest risk.
threatseverity relates to the riskscore bucket, so a riskscore from 90 to 100 gives Critical.
The sip field shows 0.0.0.0 when the request was blocked.
respsize includes the response header and payload, and totalsize is the sum of the total request size and total response size.
The url field excludes the protocol identifier, http:// or https://.

subjects.title: What a ZIA web log record is and how its fields are named

claims.statement: Some Insights names differ from the NSS meaning: reqsize appears as Sent Bytes, respsize as Received Bytes, and riskscore as Suspicious Content.
Fields without an Insights name have a blank Insights column or are marked specific to NSS, and the time-part fields are marked as derived from Logged Time.

The pcapid field holds the path of the packet capture file, formatted as company ID, directory and file name, where the directory is the log type; the file is downloaded from the Capture column of Web Insights Logs.
Web log fields describe a transaction: time is the time and date of the transaction, epochtime its epoch time, and recordid a unique record identifier for each log.
The trafficredirectmethod field records the traffic forwarding method used to reach ZIA Public Service Edges.
Each web log field is listed under an NSS format specifier and, where one exists, an Insights Logs column name; the same field can carry different names in the two places.

subjects.title: Which rule decided a web transaction, from the logs

claims.statement: `urlcat` records the category the transaction was judged under, and `urlcatmethod` records where that categorization came from, which is how logs reveal a URL's actual category membership.
`rulelabel` and `ruletype` are filled only when a Block rule applied; an allowed transaction has neither, so an empty `rulelabel` does not mean no rule matched.

URL Filtering and Cloud App Control each have their own rule-name field (`urlfilterrulelabel`, `apprulelabel`), so one record can name both when both layers evaluated, and the allow-side rule is visible there even when `rulelabel` is empty.
The `*rulelabel` fields of the NSS web log carry the name of the rule that applied, not a Rule Label object; the field list shows no field for rule labels.
